provider.provider_read_scope: Only the sanitized overview and three supplied source-code files. One attempted global find was denied; no network access, training, inference, evaluation, or data access was allowed.

observed_from_supplied_overview_and_sour: Training runs one crop per optimizer step and applies AdamW after each crop; the loss combines known-mask BCE with Dice on nonempty positive crops.
The sampler can alternate positive- and negative-centered crops; the single-image cache holds one drawing at a time, so grouping crops from one drawing can avoid repeated image loads.
The training default tile is 512 pixels while inference defaults to 896 pixels with 128-pixel overlap. Both paths require tile dimensions divisible by 64.
Labels are incomplete: the explicit known domain is authoritative and unknown pixels must be excluded from loss and selection metrics. Query/context regions are excluded.

The supplied overview reports that H1/H5 descriptor and threshold work and 200/800-update CNN continuations did not meet the desired newer development targets. These are user-provided history, not independently reproduced results.
hypotheses_not_measurements: A larger inference-aligned tile may give the model enough context to distinguish hatch textures, but may reduce resolution of fine marks and increase MPS memory use.
Four-crop accumulation may reduce update variance, but batch construction can alter document/query balance and does not itself add information.
DINOv2 features may improve semantic or pattern matching over the small CNN, but the 14-pixel patch stride may erase fine hatch boundaries and the query crop contains unmasked background.
All duration, memory, convergence, and accuracy expectations below are unverified. No training or runtime measurements were made.

protocols.name: Inference-aligned tiles with four-crop gradient accumulation
protocols.recommendation: Run a short fit-only experiment using 896x896 tiles, with two positive-centered and two known-negative-centered crops accumulated before each optimizer step. Prefer the same drawing for the four crops to reuse the current single-image cache; vary queries within that drawing when eligible. Apply one optimizer step after all four valid crop losses. Keep 512-pixel tiles and batch-1 updates as matched controls so the effects of tile size and accumulation can be separated.
code_basis: train_hatchfinder.py: DEFAULT_TILE_SIZE is 512; execute_training_step calls optimizer.step for each crop.
train_hatchfinder.py: SingleImageCache retains one drawing; CoverageSampler can cover positive/negative branches and queries.
inference_hatchfinder.py: inference tile default is 896, with overlap default 128.
protocols.proposed_schedule: Start with the existing head-only checkpoint and a fixed seed. Use a predeclared short run; if accumulation is stable, compare flat 1e-5 against a cosine schedule from 1e-5 to 1e-6 over 300 optimizer updates (1,200 valid crops), with 40 warm-up updates. These schedule values came from Gemini's proposal and are not established optima; test them only after the tile/batch comparison.
protocols.selection_gate: Create a document-grouped held-out subset from fit documents only. Score the baseline and candidates with the unchanged evaluator on identical fit-only documents. Promote only if paired document-macro IoU improves beyond a predeclared practical margin and uncertainty, while pooled recall and reviewed-negative false-positive rate stay within predeclared tolerances. Do not use public validation labels or artifacts for tuning or selection. Gemini suggested +0.025 IoU, unchanged recall, and at most 5% relative increase in empty-target FPR; treat these as provisional thresholds requiring root review, not measured standards.
risks: The 896 tile may exceed MPS memory headroom or lower the effective detail of fine hatch strokes.
A four-crop accumulated step must correctly average or sum gradients and normalize losses; empty-known or missing-class crops need explicit handling.
Sampling two positive and two negative crops within one drawing is impossible for some query rows, so eligibility and sampling balance must be documented without using unknown pixels as negatives.
Changing tile size and update batch together would confound the result; use matched controls or a small 2x2 comparison.
protocols.implementation_complexity: Low to medium; add accumulation and explicit crop grouping while retaining the existing model and checkpoint format.

duration_and_cost.provider_estimate: Gemini estimated under 80 seconds on an Apple M1 Pro for the primary trial.
duration_and_cost.confidence: Low; not measured, and data loading, 896-pixel backward memory, evaluation, and checkpoint I/O were not benchmarked.
duration_and_cost.cost: No external service cost expected for local MPS training; actual elapsed time and peak unified memory must be measured in a fit-only smoke run before scheduling the full trial.

protocols.name: Frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 patch features with a compact query-conditioned head
protocols.recommendation: Treat as a separate representation experiment if the CNN tile/accumulation trial plateaus. Freeze a licensed ViT-S/14 backbone initially and train only a small query-conditioned classifier/decoder. At 896 pixels, the 14-pixel patch grid is 64x64, so output geometry can align exactly to a tile before upsampling. Preserve the existing known-mask loss and query/context exclusions. Compare target-tile patch features conditioned on query-crop features; explicitly test query-background pooling because no query foreground mask is available. Keep local color/edge evidence or a shallow high-resolution path available to recover fine hatch boundaries.
code_basis: The task is query-conditioned mask prediction over native-resolution drawing tiles.
The existing evaluator and loss distinguish known, positive, negative, and unknown pixels; any new head must preserve those semantics.
The 896-pixel inference tile is divisible by 14, yielding a 64x64 patch map for ViT-S/14.
protocols.selection_gate: Use the same fit-only document holdout, evaluator, paired baseline, and predeclared recall/false-positive constraints as Protocol 1. First validate exact tile-to-mask alignment, query conditioning, and padding behavior on synthetic unit fixtures without labels from public validation. Proceed to model fitting only if a single-tile frozen-backbone memory/time smoke test fits the 16 GiB device budget and the feature map retains useful hatch detail.
risks: A 14-pixel patch stride may blur or miss fine hatch strokes; semantic features may not encode the local texture distinction required.
Query crops contain background and may mix relevant pattern features with unrelated drawing content.
A 64x64 feature map needs a decoder or high-resolution local branch to produce a full-resolution mask; geometry and padding must be verified.
MPS attention memory at 4,096 tokens per tile is unknown here; Gemini's stated 2.2 GiB estimate and millisecond timings are unsupported estimates and must not be used for capacity planning.
protocols.implementation_complexity: High; new backbone loading/provenance, query-feature pooling, a pixel-mask decoder or high-resolution refinement path, and inference/checkpoint integration are required.

duration_and_cost.provider_estimate: Gemini estimated roughly 2.0–2.5 minutes for 300 updates and about 2.2 GiB peak unified memory.
duration_and_cost.confidence: Very low; not measured, and the estimate's exact architecture and MPS attention implementation are not verified.
duration_and_cost.cost: Local inference/training has no API cost. Weight download size, actual MPS memory, and duration must be measured before adoption.

protocols.name: Matched late-encoder unfreezing with a lower learning rate
protocols.recommendation: Only after a fit-only comparison shows the current head-only representation is the limiting factor, compare head-only training against unfreezing the final encoder stage with a substantially smaller encoder learning rate than the prediction head. Keep the optimizer, crop sequence, tile size, and number of optimizer updates fixed across the pair.
code_basis: train_hatchfinder.py exposes head and all trainable scopes, but its current optimizer uses one learning rate for all trainable parameters.
The supplied history reports that longer 200/800-update continuations did not improve the newer development targets, so simply increasing update count is not a useful next experiment.
protocols.selection_gate: Same fit-only document holdout and paired metrics as Protocol 1. Reject if improvement is limited to training loss or if recall/negative false-positive constraints regress.
risks: The existing all-scope option updates many more parameters and may overfit the modest fit set.
Separate learning-rate groups, checkpoint metadata, and reproducible initialization are required; do not attribute a difference to encoder unfreezing if crop order or schedule also changes.
protocols.implementation_complexity: Medium; add parameter groups and record the scope and per-group learning rates in provenance.

duration_and_cost.estimate: Unknown until a short MPS memory/time benchmark. This option may cost more than head-only training; do not infer runtime from the 200/800-step history.
